heroData.title: Hire in Brazil (No Entity)
heroData.subtitle: CLT Compliance
heroData.description: Hire employees without a local Ltda. EOR handles the complex 'Custo Brasil' (approx +70-80% on top of salary).

steps.title: Medical Exam (ASO)
steps.description: Mandatory admission exam (Atestado de Saúde Ocupacional). Must be done BEFORE the start date.

steps.title: Document Collection
steps.description: CPF, RG, PIS/PASEP number, Proof of Address, Voter Title, Military Certificate (men).

steps.title: eSocial Registration
steps.description: Employer must register the admission event (S-2200) in the federal system by the day before start date.

steps.title: CTPS Digital
steps.description: Update the employee's Digital Work Card (Carteira de Trabalho Digital) with contract details.

steps.title: Benefits Enrollment
steps.description: Setup Vale Transporte (Transport), Vale Refeição (Meal), and Health Insurance plans.

items.title: CLT vs. PJ
items.text: CLT is the standard employment contract. Hiring individuals as 'PJ' (Legal Entity/Contractor) to avoid taxes is illegal if subordination exists ('Pejotização'). Fines are massive.

items.title: Probation Period
items.text: Maximum 90 days. Usually split as 45 + 45 days. Termination costs are lower during this period.

items.title: Remote Work (Teletrabalho)
items.text: Since 2022, specific laws govern remote work. Contracts must specify if the role is 'totally remote' or 'hybrid' to determine benefit obligations.

faqs.question: Can I hire contractors indefinitely?
faqs.answer: No. If a contractor works full-time, exclusively, and under your direct supervision, Labor Courts will reclassify them as employees.

faqs.question: What is the 13th Month Salary?
faqs.answer: A mandatory bonus equal to one month's salary, paid in two installments (November and December).

faqs.question: Is notice period paid?
faqs.answer: Yes. 'Aviso Prévio' is minimally 30 days, plus 3 days for every year of service, capped at 90 days.

faqs.question: What happens if I fire an employee?
faqs.answer: Without cause, you pay all accrued rights PLUS a 40% penalty on the total historic FGTS balance.

faqs.question: Are background checks legal?
faqs.answer: Generally restricted to specific roles (e.g., handling money, security). Criminal checks for standard office jobs can be considered discriminatory.

items.title: TST (Labor Court)
items.text: Superior Labor Court rulings and precedents.

items.title: Gov.br - eSocial
items.text: Official portal for the eSocial reporting system.

items.title: CLT
items.text: Consolidação das Leis do Trabalho - The primary labor law code.

items.title: Carteira de Trabalho (CTPS)
items.text: The official work history document for every Brazilian.

items.title: Dissídio
items.text: Annual salary adjustment negotiated by the Union.

items.title: DSR
items.text: Descanso Semanal Remunerado. A paid rest day (usually Sunday) included in the monthly salary.

items.title: Personal Relationships
items.text: Business is personal. Expect small talk (football, family, food) before meetings start. Rushing to business is considered rude.

items.title: Flexible Time
items.text: Punctuality is flexible for social events, but increasingly strict for business meetings in São Paulo. In other regions, 10-15 min delays are normal.

items.title: Physical Contact
items.text: Greetings often involve handshakes with eye contact. In less formal settings, a kiss on the cheek (one or two depending on the state) is common.

items.text: Greetings often involve handshakes with eye contact. In less formal settings, a kiss on the cheek (one or two depending on the state) is common.

steps.title: Day 20 (Adiantamento)
steps.description: Optional but common. 40% salary advance paid to employees for the current month.

steps.title: Day 30/31 (Closing)
steps.description: Payroll period closes. Overtime and commissions calculated.

steps.title: Day 5 (Payment)
steps.description: Legal deadline to pay the remaining balance (Salário) is the 5th BUSINESS day of the following month.

steps.title: Day 7 (FGTS)
steps.description: Deadline to deposit 8% FGTS into Caixa Econômica Federal accounts.

steps.title: Day 20 (Taxes)
steps.description: Deadline to pay INSS (DARF Previdenciário) and IRRF (Income Tax Withheld).

rows: Capped at this level (Teto do INSS).

items.title: Vale Transporte
items.text: Employer must cover transport costs exceeding 6% of employee's basic salary.

items.title: Vale Refeição/Alimentação
items.text: Meal vouchers. Not legally mandatory but functionally required to attract talent. Tax-deductible if registered with PAT program.

items.title: Vacation Bonus
items.text: When taking 30 days vacation, employee receives their normal salary PLUS 1/3 extra (Terço de Férias).

faqs.question: What is the 13th Salary?
faqs.answer: A mandatory extra month of salary. 1st installment (50%) by Nov 30th, 2nd installment (balance) by Dec 20th.

faqs.question: Can I pay in USD?
faqs.answer: No. Brazilian labor contracts must be denominated and paid in BRL (Real) in a local account.

faqs.question: Is overtime mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes. Standard is +50% for weekdays, +100% for Sundays/Holidays. Managers/Directors may be exempt.

faqs.question: What is PAT?
faqs.answer: Workers' Food Program. Registering meal benefits here exempts them from being considered 'salary' for tax purposes.

faqs.question: What is eSocial?
faqs.answer: A unified digital reporting system. Payroll data is transmitted directly to the government. Errors trigger automatic fines.

items.title: Receita Federal
items.text: Tax tables and DARF generation.

items.title: Caixa - FGTS
items.text: Official FGTS guidelines for employers.

items.title: Holerite
items.text: Payslip.

items.title: Adicional Noturno
items.text: Night shift bonus (+20%) for work between 10 PM and 5 AM.

items.title: Periculosidade
items.text: Hazard pay (+30%) for dangerous jobs (electricity, security, flammables).

steps.title: Step 1: Variables
steps.description: Gather all overtime hours, sales commissions, and absences by the 25th.

steps.title: Step 2: Advance (Vale)
steps.description: If company policy dictates, pay the 'Adiantamento' (40%) on the 15th or 20th.

steps.title: Step 3: Calculate
steps.description: Process the payroll calculation. Apply INSS and IRRF tables. Deduct VT/VR co-participation.

steps.title: Step 4: Transmit
steps.description: Send events S-1200 (Remuneration) and S-1210 (Payments) to eSocial.

steps.title: Step 5: FGTS
steps.description: Generate the FGTS slip (Guias) and pay by the 7th.

steps.title: Step 6: Taxes
steps.description: Generate and pay the DCTFWeb/DARF by the 20th.

steps.title: Step 7: Payslips
steps.description: Distribute Holerites (Payslips) to employees digitally or physically (must be signed/acknowledged).

steps.title: Gross Salary Definition
steps.description: Determine the monthly base salary in BRL. Remember that CLT workers receive 13.33 salaries per year (12 months + 13th salary + 1/3 vacation bonus).

steps.title: Mandatory Benefit Selection
steps.description: Add costs for Meal Allowance (VR/VA), Transport Vouchers (VT), and Life Insurance. These vary based on the Collective Bargaining Agreement (CCT).

steps.title: Tax & Social Contribution Calculation
steps.description: Calculate Employer FGTS (8%), Social Security contributions (rate depends on tax regime), and provision for severance and vacations.

items.title: The 80% Rule
items.text: For a safe budget, add 70-80% on top of the gross salary to cover taxes, benefits, 13th month, vacation, and severance accruals.

items.title: Simples Companies
items.text: For small companies on 'Simples Nacional', the burden is lower (approx 40% on top of salary).

faqs.question: Does this include office costs?
faqs.answer: No. This multiplier covers only statutory labor costs and mandatory benefits.

faqs.question: Is health insurance mandatory?
faqs.answer: Not by federal law, but often mandatory by Union Convention (CCT). Check the specific union rules.

items.title: Union Fees
items.text: Patronal Union fees are mandatory in January. Employee union fees depend on opposition letters.

items.title: Termination Fine
items.text: Remember the 40% FGTS penalty. It's not a tax, it's a direct cost to the employer upon firing without cause.

items.title: VT (Transport)
items.text: Employer pays everything above 6% of the employee's salary. In big cities with expensive transit, this adds up.

items.title: São Paulo
items.text: Benchmark 100%. Highest salaries, highest office costs, highest meal allowance expectations.

items.title: South (Curitiba/Floripa)
items.text: Approx 85-90% of SP costs. High quality of life, good English.

items.title: Northeast (Recife/Salvador)
items.text: Approx 60-75% of SP costs. Growing tech scene, very competitive rates.

heroData.title: Ltda vs S.A.
heroData.subtitle: Local Partner Needed
heroData.description: Ltda (Sociedade Limitada) is most common. Requires a local resident admin (Director) or Power of Attorney holder.

steps.title: Step 1: Viability
steps.description: Viabilidade Locacional. Check if the business address permits the specific commercial activity (CNAE).

steps.title: Step 2: DBBE
steps.description: Documento Básico de Entrada. Filing with the Redesim (Federal Network).

steps.title: Step 3: Articles (Contrato Social)
steps.description: Drafting and signing the Articles of Association. Foreign partners need apostilled/translated docs.

steps.title: Step 4: Registration (Junta)
steps.description: File with the State Board of Trade (Junta Comercial). Gives you the NIRE number.

steps.title: Step 5: CNPJ
steps.description: Federal Tax ID issuance. Enables bank account opening.

steps.title: Step 6: Inscrição Municipal
steps.description: City registration for Service Tax (ISS) and operating license (Alvará).

items.title: Legal Representative
items.text: You MUST have a resident in Brazil (Brazilian or foreigner with permanent visa) to act as the administrator. They carry personal liability.

items.title: UBO Disclosure
items.text: Ultimate Beneficial Owners (individuals) must be disclosed to the Receita Federal to prevent money laundering.

items.title: Virtual Office
items.text: Accepted for service companies. Mandatory physical address for retail/industrial.

items.title: Ltda (Limitada)
items.text: Equivalent to LLC. Simple governance. Liability limited to quota capital. Most common for subsidiaries.

items.title: S.A. (Sociedade Anônima)
items.text: Corporation. More strict publication/audit rules. Required for banking/insurance sectors or pre-IPO.

items.title: EIRELI (Defunct)
items.text: Replaced by SLU (Sociedade Limitada Unipersonal) - Single member LLC.

faqs.question: Minimum Capital?
faqs.answer: None for Ltda (theoretically R$ 1). However, banks prefer R$ 10k-50k for account opening.

faqs.question: Can foreigners own 100%?
faqs.answer: Yes. A foreign entity can own 99% and a foreign individual 1%, or just one foreign entity (via SLU).

faqs.question: How long to open a bank account?
faqs.answer: The hardest part. Top tier banks (Itaú, Bradesco) take 1-3 months for foreign-owned entities. FinTechs (Inter, Nubank PJ) are faster but strict.

faqs.question: Do I need a physical office?
faqs.answer: For service companies, a 'Fiscal Address' (virtual office) is sufficient. For goods/trade, you need a warehouse/physical location.

faqs.question: What is the cost?
faqs.answer: Legal fees + Filing fees vary. Budget approx $5k-$10k USD for the full setup including legal representation.

items.text: Articles of Association/bylaws for a Ltda.

steps.title: Address Proof
steps.description: Secure a commercial address and get the IPTU (Property Tax) booklet cover.

steps.title: Articles Draft
steps.description: Lawyer drafts 'Contrato Social'. Define capital, activities, and administration.

items.title: Traditional Banks (Big 5)
items.text: Itaú, Bradesco, Santander, Banco do Brasil, Caixa. pros: robust, full service. cons: bureaucratic, high fees, slow API.

items.title: Digital Banks
items.text: Nubank PJ, Inter, Cora. pros: free, fast, good APIs. cons: limited for international FX or complex credit.

items.title: FX Registration
items.text: To receive capital from abroad, you must close an exchange contract (Fechamento de Câmbio). Choose a bank with a good FX desk.

items.title: Model A1
items.text: Digital file valid for 1 year. Installed on computers/servers. Best for automation and SaaS integration.

items.title: Model A3
items.text: Physical token/card valid for 3 years. Harder to use with cloud software as it requires USB connection.

items.title: Requirement
items.text: Mandatory for issuing invoices (NF-e) and accessing eSocial/Conectividade Social.

heroData.title: Corporate Tax
heroData.subtitle: Complex System
heroData.description: Standard 'Lucro Real' or 'Lucro Presumido'. Taxes include IRPJ, CSLL, PIS, COFINS, ISS.

items.title: Lucro Real
items.text: Actual Profit. Mandatory for revenue > R$ 78m or finance companies. Tax based on audited net profit. PIS/COFINS are non-cumulative (9.25%).

items.title: Lucro Presumido
items.text: Presumed Profit. For revenue < R$ 78m. Tax base is a presumption of profit (e.g., 32% for services). PIS/COFINS are cumulative (3.65%) but no credits.

items.title: Simples Nacional
items.text: Unified tax for small businesses (Rev < R$ 4.8m). One single monthly slip (DAS).

items.title: Dual VAT (IVA Dual)
items.text: PIS, COFINS, and IPI will merge into CBS (Federal). ICMS and ISS will merge into IBS (Sub-national). Transition begins 2026.

items.title: Simplification?
items.text: Long term yes. Short term (2026-2032) involves running parallel systems. Compliance costs will spike during transition.

items.title: DARF
items.text: Documento de Arrecadação de Receitas Federais - The slip used to pay federal taxes.

items.title: Nota Fiscal (NF-e)
items.text: Electronic invoice. Mandatory validation with the government for every B2B/B2C sale.

items.title: Substituição Tributária (ST)
items.text: Tax Substitution. Manufacturer pays VAT on behalf of the entire supply chain.

steps.title: Monthly: Day 20
steps.description: PIS, COFINS, and CSLL payments due (for previous month).

steps.title: Monthly: Day 20
steps.description: Social Security (INSS) payment due.

steps.title: Quarterly
steps.description: IRPJ (Corporate Income Tax) calculation and payment for Lucro Presumido.

steps.title: Annual: May
steps.description: ECD (Digital Accounting) submission deadline.

steps.title: Annual: July
steps.description: ECF (Fiscal Accounting) submission deadline.

steps.title: Annual: Feb
steps.description: DIRF (Withholding Tax Report) - being phased out but still relevant.

faqs.question: What is the total tax burden?
faqs.answer: Effective corporate tax rate averages around 34% on profits, plus ~10-15% on gross revenue for sales taxes.

faqs.question: Are dividends taxed?
faqs.answer: Currently NO (0% WHT). However, new legislation constantly proposes taxing dividends at 15%. Check current status.

faqs.question: Does Brazil have tax treaties?
faqs.answer: Yes, with ~35 countries to avoid double taxation, but NOT with the United States.

faqs.question: What is Transfer Pricing?
faqs.answer: Brazil recently aligned with OECD standards (2024), moving away from fixed margins to the arm's length principle.

items.title: DPO (Encarregado)
items.text: Companies must appoint a Data Protection Officer. Their contact must be public on the site.

items.title: Rights
items.text: Citizens have rights to access, delete, and correct data. Response time is 15 days.

items.title: Fines
items.text: Up to 2% of revenue, capped at R$ 50M per infraction.

steps.title: Track Time
steps.description: Strictly track hours. Overtime claims are the #1 lawsuit trigger.

steps.title: Avoid 'Pj'
steps.description: Do not treat contractors like employees. No fixed hours, no direct subordination, no personal exclusivity.

steps.title: Health & Safety
steps.description: Maintain PPRA (Risk Prevention) and PCMSO (Medical Control) programs up to date.

items.title: CIPA
items.text: Internal Commission for Accident Prevention. Mandatory for larger companies.

items.title: Sindicato
items.text: Labor Union. Every employee belongs to a category union based on the company's main activity.

faqs.question: What is the 'Custo Brasil'?
faqs.answer: A term referring to the structural costs of doing business: bureaucracy, complex taxes, infrastructure gaps, and legal risks.

faqs.question: Can I fire a pregnant employee?
faqs.answer: Absolutely not. They have stability from conception until 5 months after birth.

faqs.question: Is arbitration accepted?
faqs.answer: Yes, for higher level contracts (remuneration > 2x limit), arbitration clauses are enforceable.

faqs.question: Can I work on a tourist visa?
faqs.answer: Legally, no. You cannot receive remuneration from a Brazilian source.

faqs.question: How long is the process?
faqs.answer: Work visas take 30-45 days for approval from the Ministry of Justice.

steps.title: PCMSO / PPRA / LTCAT
steps.description: Verify if all Health & Safety reports are renewed annually.

steps.title: CIPA
steps.description: Check if Internal Accident Prevention Commission election was held (if required).

steps.title: Union Dues
steps.description: Confirm payment of 'Contribuição Sindical' (if opted in) and 'Assistencial'.

steps.title: FGTS Certificate
steps.description: Pull the CRF (Certificado de Regularidade do FGTS) monthly to ensure good standing.

steps.title: CND Federal
steps.description: Check Certidão Negativa de Débitos regularly to avoid surprises.

steps.title: Eligibility
steps.description: Work for a foreign employer (non-Brazilian). Valid for 1 year, renewable for 1 more.

steps.title: Income Req
steps.description: Proof of income > US$ 1,500/month OR bank funds > US$ 18,000.

steps.title: Application
steps.description: Apply at a Brazilian Consulate abroad or via MigranteWeb if already in Brazil.

items.title: Sponsorship
items.text: Requires a Brazilian entity to sponsor. The entity must prove no local candidate was found (Labor Market Test) unless for specialized tech roles.

items.title: RN 13/2017 (Investor)
items.text: Granting residency for investing R$ 500k (or R$ 150k in innovation) requires a business plan proving job creation.

steps.title: Step 1: Doc Prep
steps.description: Gather birth certificates, police clearance, and marriage certs. Apostille EVERYTHING in home country.

steps.title: Step 2: RN Check
steps.description: Identify the correct Normative Resolution (RN) for your case (e.g., RN 45 for Nomads).

steps.title: Step 3: MigranteWeb
steps.description: Upload documents to the Ministry of Justice system (if in Brazil) or submit to Consulate.

steps.title: Step 4: Approval
steps.description: Wait for the DOU (Diário Oficial da União) publication of approval.

steps.title: Step 5: Registration
steps.description: Upon arrival/approval, visit Federal Police within 90 days to release the CRNM (ID Card).

items.title: CRNM
items.text: Carteira de Registro Nacional Migratório. The physical ID card for foreigners.

items.title: CPF for Foreigners
items.text: You can (and should) get a CPF even before the visa. Apply at a Brazilian consulate or online.

items.title: Overstay Fine
items.text: Daily fine for overstaying tourist visa. Must be paid before re-entry.

items.title: Mandatory Accountant
items.text: It is legally impossible to run a company without a registered accountant (CRC) co-signing your filings.

items.title: SPED
items.text: Public Digital Bookkeeping System. Accounting files (ECD, ECF) are digitally signed and transmitted to the Receita.

faqs.question: What is a 'Nota Fiscal'?
faqs.answer: An official invoice generated via government software. No payment is valid without it.

faqs.question: Can I use Xero/Quickbooks?
faqs.answer: Not directly for statutory compliance. You need local software (ContaAzul, Omie) or a bridge to handle Brazilian tax codes.

faqs.question: What is the fiscal year?
faqs.answer: Starts Jan 1st, ends Dec 31st. Matches the calendar year.

steps.title: ECF (Fiscal)
steps.description: Escrituração Contábil Fiscal. Replaces the old income tax return. Due in July.

steps.title: ECD (Digital)
steps.description: Escrituração Contábil Digital. The digital version of the Daily Journal and General Ledger. Due in May.

steps.title: DIRF
steps.description: Withholding Income Tax Declaration. Verify all employee and contractor retentions. Due in Feb.

steps.title: DEFIS
steps.description: For 'Simples Nacional' companies only. Simplified annual declaration.

steps.title: RAIS
steps.description: Annual Report of Social Information. Crucial for government labor statistics and 'Abono Salarial' payment.

items.title: COFINS
items.text: Contribution for Social Security Financing. A federal tax on gross revenue.

items.title: PIS
items.text: Social Integration Program. Federal tax on revenue, often paired with COFINS.

items.title: ISS
items.text: Imposto Sobre Serviços. Municipal Service Tax (2% to 5%). Varies by city and service type.

items.title: IRPJ
items.text: Corporate Income Tax. 15% base + 10% surcharge on profits > R$ 20k/month.

items.title: CSLL
items.text: Social Contribution on Net Profit. Usually 9%.

heroData.title: HR Tech
heroData.subtitle: Point Control
heroData.description: Digital time tracking (Ponto Eletrônico) is mandatory for companies with >20 employees.

items.title: Portaria 671
items.text: Regulates electronic point control (REP). Systems must be certified and tamper-proof.

items.title: Apps
items.text: Mobile punch-in apps are legal (REP-A or REP-P) but must record GPS location.

faqs.question: Is Workday/BambooHR compliant?
faqs.answer: For data storage, yes. For payroll calculation and taxes, NO. They usually integrate with a local engine (ADP, TMF).

faqs.question: Must I track lunch breaks?
faqs.answer: Yes. The system must record the 'Intervalo Intrajornada' (usually 1 hour).

steps.title: Parameterization
steps.description: Configure shifts, overtime rules (50% vs 100%), and grace periods (usually 10 min tolerance).

steps.title: Employee Sync
steps.description: Import employee data (PIS number is crucial for consistency) from payroll.

steps.title: biometric/App
steps.description: Register biometrics or setup app geo-fencing requirements.

steps.title: Parallel Run
steps.description: Run the new system alongside the old one for 1 month to catch calculation errors.

steps.title: Integration
steps.description: Test the export file (AFD/AFDT) for import into the payroll software (Folha de Pagamento).

items.title: REP-C
items.text: Registrador Eletrônico de Ponto Convencional. The traditional wall-mounted biometric clock.

items.title: REP-A
items.text: Alternative Electronic Point Recorder. Authorized by collective bargaining (CCT). Flexible software solutions.

items.title: REP-P
items.text: Program Electronic Point Recorder. Software registered with INPI. The modern standard for SaaS HRIS.

items.title: Pontomais
items.text: Market leader for digital time tracking. Strong integration ecosystem.

items.title: Tangerino
items.text: Another strong contender, focus on mobile interactions and facial recognition.

heroData.title: Tech Recruitment
heroData.subtitle: LATAM Hub
heroData.description: Brazil is the largest tech talent pool in LATAM. Strong in Java, Python, and Mobile dev.

items.title: São Paulo (SP)
items.text: The financial capital. Most expensive, but highest concentration of senior talent and English speakers.

items.title: Florianópolis (SC)
items.text: Tech island. High quality of life, strong dev community, slightly lower costs than SP.

items.title: Belo Horizonte (MG)
items.text: Startup hub (San Pedro Valley). Excellent engineering universities (UFMG).

items.title: Speed
items.text: Good devs get multiple offers. Hiring process should be < 2 weeks.

items.title: English
items.text: English proficiency is low generally (<5%), but in senior tech circles it's common. Verify with a conversational interview.

faqs.question: What is the typical agency fee?
faqs.answer: 15-25% of the first year's annual gross salary.

faqs.question: Is non-compete enforceable?
faqs.answer: Very difficult. Courts favor the 'right to work'. Only enforceable if compensable (paid during the non-compete period) and geographically limited.

steps.title: Job Spec
steps.description: Define role and stack. Brazilians value clear descriptions.

steps.title: Sourcing
steps.description: Use LinkedIn (dominant) and local platforms like Gupy.

steps.title: Screening
steps.description: Test English early. Technical test (coding) is standard.

steps.title: Offer
steps.description: Present offer in Gross Monthly Salary (BRL/month), not annual.

steps.title: Onboarding
steps.description: Collect documents (CTPS, ID, Address Proof) for eSocial registration.

items.title: CLT
items.text: Consolidação das Leis do Trabalho. Full-time employment with all benefits.

items.title: PJ
items.text: Pessoa Jurídica. Contractor arrangement (B2B). Higher risks but higher net pay for seniors.

items.title: Pleno
items.text: Mid-level developer. Usually 3-5 years of experience.

heroData.title: Digital Marketing
heroData.subtitle: Highly Social
heroData.description: Brazilians are among the world's heaviest social media users (Instagram, WhatsApp, TikTok).

items.title: WhatsApp
items.text: Ubiquitous. Used for B2C sales, customer support, and even B2B negotiations.

items.title: Instagram
items.text: Huge for e-commerce and brand validation. Influencer marketing is very mature.

items.title: Influencers
items.text: Micro-influencers often deliver better ROI than massive celebs.

steps.title: Regional Audience Mapping
steps.description: Identify target demographics across Brazil's diverse regions (Southeast, South, Northeast). Tailor messaging to local cultural nuances and purchasing power.

steps.title: Portuguese Content Localization
steps.description: Translate and adapt all marketing materials into Brazilian Portuguese (PT-BR). Ensure tone and vocabulary resonate with the local market.

steps.title: WhatsApp Sales Funnel Setup
steps.description: Integrate WhatsApp into the customer journey. Set up automated responses and human-assisted sales flows to capitalize on Brazil's preferred channel.

faqs.question: Do I need Portuguese?
faqs.answer: Yes. 100%. English content will not convert in the mass market.

faqs.question: What is LGPD for marketing?
faqs.answer: You need explicit consent (opt-in) for email marketing. Purchasing lists is illegal and risky.

items.title: Humor & Memes
items.text: Brazilians love humor and memes. Brands that master 'zueira' (playfulness) on Twitter/Insta gain high engagement.

items.title: Seasonality
items.text: Respect Carnival (Feb/Mar) and São João (June). These are massive cultural moments, not just holidays.

items.title: Inclusivity
items.text: Brazil is extremely diverse. Advertising should reflect the pardo, black, and white population mix authentically.

items.title: Tráfego Pago
items.text: Paid Traffic (Ads). Extremely competitive on FB/Insta/Google.

items.title: Lançamento
items.text: Launch Formula. A specific high-pressure sales funnel strategy very popular in Brazil.

items.title: Influenciador
items.text: Influencer. Brazil has one of the highest trust rates in influencers globally.

heroData.title: Legal & Contracts
heroData.subtitle: MSA & Agreements
heroData.description: Standard Master Service Agreements (MSA) and localized employment contracts for Brazil. Ensuring compliance with CLT (Consolidation of Labor Laws).

items.title: Written Contracts
items.text: While verbal contracts are valid, written contracts are essential for proving specific terms like confidentiality and non-compete.

items.title: Language
items.text: Contracts must be in Portuguese to be legally binding and enforceable in Brazilian courts.

items.title: Indemnity
items.text: Limitation of liability is generally accepted in B2B but strictly scrutinized in consumer/labor contexts.

faqs.question: Are e-signatures valid?
faqs.answer: Yes, via ICP-Brasil (standard digital certificate) or platforms like DocuSign/Adobe Sign if agreed by both parties.

faqs.question: What is Forum Selection?
faqs.answer: Parties can choose a specific city/court for disputes, but labor claims ALWAYS stay in the city where the employee worked.

faqs.question: Do I need a local lawyer?
faqs.answer: Yes. Only lawyers registered with the OAB (Brazilian Bar) can practice law or sign corporate documents in Brazil.

steps.title: Translations
steps.description: Ensure bilingual format (PT/EN) if needed for HQ management.

steps.title: Notice Periods
steps.description: Verify that notice periods align with CLT minimums (30+ days).

steps.title: IP Clause
steps.description: Explicitly state that all creations during work hours belong to the employer.

heroData.title: Software Localization
heroData.subtitle: Tropicalization
heroData.description: Adapting software for Brazil (CPF fields, Boleto payments, Translation).

items.title: CPF/CNPJ Field
items.text: Essential. Brazilian forms must validate CPF (11 digits) or CNPJ (14 digits). Verify check digits.

items.title: Address Forms
items.text: Use CEP (Postal Code). Users expect auto-fill of Street, City, State upon entering the 8-digit CEP.

items.title: Payment Methods
items.text: Must support Pix and Boleto. Credit cards often require 'Parcelamento' (Installments) support even for small purchases.

steps.title: Language & Cultural Translation
steps.description: Localize the interface to PT-BR. Adjust for local formats: date (DD/MM/YYYY), currency (R$), and decimal separators (comma for decimals).

steps.title: Statutory Data Validation
steps.description: Implement algorithms for real-time validation of CPF (individuals) and CNPJ (entities). Failure to validate these leads to high churn and registration issues.

steps.title: Local Payment Integration
steps.description: Integrate Pix (instant transfer) and Boleto Bancário (cash-friendly bank slips). Without Pix, conversion rates in Brazil drop significantly.

faqs.question: Is WhatsApp integration needed?
faqs.answer: Highly recommended. A 'Click to WhatsApp' button converts better than email forms.

faqs.question: What about language?
faqs.answer: Use PT-BR (Brazilian Portuguese), not PT-PT (European). The difference in vocabulary is significant.

items.title: Mercado Livre
items.text: The Amazon of Latin America. Dominant marketplace. Integration is key for retail software.

items.title: Pix Payments
items.text: Instant payments system by Central Bank. Now accounts for massive share of e-commerce txns. Must have 'Copy & Paste' code.

items.title: Logistics
items.text: Shipping is expensive and slow outside capitals. Correios is the default, but private carriers (Loggi) are growing.

items.title: San Pedro Valley
items.text: Belo Horizonte (MG). Known for high density of startups and exits (Hotmart).

items.title: Porto Digital
items.text: Recife (PE). A major tech park in the northeast, strong in software outsourcing.

items.title: Cubo Itaú
items.text: São Paulo (SP). Largest innovation hub in LatAm, great for B2B connections.
